_doc: The language of each theme, in three tiers. `named` is what a person inside that world recognises on sight — dishes, dances, games, acts, records, roles, rites. `said` is what they actually say: jargon, verbs, terms of art. `voice` is supporting texture and is never a board's reason to exist. Filtered at scoring time to ENABLE1 + popular + 3..6 letters AND NO REPEATED LETTER, because a base is six DISTINCT letters and cannot spell `cool`, `greens` or `grill`.
_rule: A word earns a place here only if someone inside the theme would say it — NOT a list of objects visible at the scene. The cultural bench requires this file reviewed BEFORE any base is scored, objects capped at roughly a quarter of a list, and pack floors of 12 / caps of 20 set by judgment, because raw yield rewards ordinary vocabulary and punishes specificity.
_size: LIST GENEROUSLY. Board count scales super-linearly with usable vocabulary: rnb90s at 145 usable words yields 63 boards, cookout at 53 yields 3. A thin list looks like a thin theme and is not one — that misreading has already been made twice in this project. Over-listing costs nothing; the filter discards what the build cannot serve.
_rnb90s_note: LOCKED and shipped. Two earlier drafts failed: the first led with label/master/credit/royalties, which the cultural bench blocked as documentary grievance-talk centring the business over the music and writing the women out of a decade they authored; the second led with craft nouns, true but generic. Entries are cut unless the word literally appears in the act or title: `escape` is NOT Xscape and `level` is NOT LeVert.
